evidence.title: Parks Associates: 16% of US internet households have a smart thermostat

verdicts.reading: In 2020 Western tech firms are bound by norms such that helping an authoritarian government monitor or block protesters brings significant penalties in other markets.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Whether Western firms supplying censorship or monitoring to authoritarian states faced significant penalties by 2020.
verdicts.reason: No such norm bound firms in 2020: Sandvine (North American) equipment was used by Belarus in 2020 to cut internet during protests and by Egypt, Turkey and others for censorship; the first US penalty (Entity List) came only in Feb 2024 and was lifted in Oct 2024.

evidence.title: Sandvine (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Equipment used for Belarus 2020 shutdowns and Egyptian censorship; Entity List only in Feb 2024, removed Oct 2024.

verdicts.reading: By 2020 large-dataset analysis, including nowcasting, improves social, political and economic intelligence, and Big Data is a huge net positive for society.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Routine use of big-data nowcasting by economic institutions by 2020 (at least 20% of central banks/agencies); the net-positive part has no measure.
verdicts.reason: The factual half held: nowcasting became routine at central banks (Atlanta Fed GDPNow from 2014, NY Fed nowcast) and expanded to alternative data. The 'huge positive in nearly all respects' half is a value judgment with no public measure, and was contested (privacy, Cambridge Analytica). Graded on the measurable half as partial.

evidence.title: Nowcasting (economics) (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Central banks are primary users; GDPNow launched 2014, NY Fed dynamic factor nowcast; ML and social data added.

verdicts.reading: By 2020 higher education is quite different, with mass adoption of distance learning and hybrid classes and more customized graduation outcomes.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16: share of US postsecondary students in any distance-education course at least 20% by 2022.
verdicts.reason: Distance learning was mainstream before the pandemic (36% of undergraduates and 42% of postbaccalaureate students in fall 2019) and reached 75% in fall 2020. Customized graduation requirements did not broadly arrive, but the core adoption held.

evidence.title: NCES Fast Facts: Distance learning (postsecondary)
evidence.shows: Undergraduates in any distance course: 36% fall 2019, 75% fall 2020; postbaccalaureate 42% and 71%.

verdicts.reading: By 2025 the Internet of Things has widespread and beneficial effects on everyday life.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16: connected home/personal IoT devices in at least 20% of households in major markets by 2025-2027.
verdicts.reason: IoT is widespread: 18.5B connected IoT devices in 2024, ~21B forecast for 2025; about a third of US broadband households owned a smart-home device by 2021 and ~21% of adults a wearable by 2019. 'Beneficial' is a value judgment not graded; the adoption part is clearly met.

evidence.title: IoT Analytics, Number of connected IoT devices
evidence.shows: 18.5B connected IoT devices in 2024, 21.1B expected end-2025.

evidence.title: Parks Associates: 34% of US broadband households own a smart home device
evidence.shows: 34% of US broadband households own a smart-home device; 23% own three or more.

verdicts.reading: By 2025 there will be no significant changes for the worse in how people get and share content online compared with 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Global internet freedom trend 2014-2025 (Freedom on the Net: blocking, arrests, content limits).
verdicts.reason: Conditions worsened significantly: Freedom House recorded 14 consecutive years of decline to 2024, website blocking of political/social/religious speech in at least 41 countries, arrests for online expression in 56 of 72 countries, and content-limit scores at their lowest in more than a decade.

evidence.title: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2024
evidence.shows: 14th consecutive year of decline; blocking in 41+ countries; arrests in 56 of 72; content limits at decade low.

verdicts.reading: By 2025 AI and robotics will not have displaced more jobs than they created.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Net employment in major economies in 2025 (e.g. US unemployment rate near historic lows, employment at record levels).
verdicts.reason: No net job loss: US unemployment stayed at 4.0-4.4% through 2025, near historic lows, and employment was at record levels; no major economy showed AI-driven net job destruction by 2025.

evidence.title: BLS, Civilian unemployment rate
evidence.shows: US unemployment 4.0% (Jan 2025) to 4.4% (Sep 2025).

verdicts.reading: By 2025 a major cyberattack has caused widespread harm to a nation's security, with significant loss of life or losses in the tens of billions of dollars.
verdicts.mainstream_test: A single cyberattack by 2025 with losses on the order of $10B+ that harmed a nation's security and defensive capacity.
verdicts.reason: NotPetya (2017), attributed to Russian military intelligence, hit Ukrainian ministries, banks, metro and state enterprises and knocked Chernobyl radiation monitoring offline, with total damage put at over $10B by the US Homeland Security adviser - 'the most destructive and costly cyberattack in history'. That meets the stated scale at its lower bound.

evidence.title: 2017 Ukraine ransomware attacks (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: NotPetya: >$10B damage; Ukrainian ministries, banks, metro, state firms hit; attributed to Russia's GRU.

verdicts.reading: By 2025 there will be no secure, popularly accepted and trusted privacy-rights infrastructure giving individuals easy control over their data.
verdicts.mainstream_test: Public trust and sense of control over personal data in 2023-2025 (US), and existence of a comprehensive framework.
verdicts.reason: No trusted infrastructure emerged: in 2023, 73% of Americans felt little or no control over company data, only 20% trusted data holders to act responsibly, 72% wanted more regulation; the US still had no federal privacy law. The 'no' view held.

evidence.title: Pew Research Center, How Americans View Data Privacy
evidence.shows: 73% little/no control over company data; 20% trust holders; 72% want more regulation.

verdicts.reading: Changes set in motion by COVID-19 make life in 2025 mostly worse for most people than at the start of the pandemic.
verdicts.mainstream_test: A public measure of whether life is better or worse for most people in 2025 than in early 2020, attributable to pandemic-driven change.
verdicts.reason: A whole-of-life value judgment (like the D27 'net effect' example). Looked for UNDP Human Development Index data: the 2023/24 report describes recovery to record global HDI but uneven, with many poorer countries below pre-pandemic paths; no measure isolates pandemic-driven change or 'most people's' lives.

evidence.title: UNDP, Human Development Report 2023/24
evidence.shows: Post-pandemic recovery uneven and rising inequality; no measure of 'mostly worse for most people' due to pandemic changes.
